facts.text: University of Michigan researchers Zhao, Peng and colleagues used importance sampling in 2016 to make rare crash and conflict events more frequent in simulation and statistically reweight the results.
facts.quote: University of Michigan researchers (Zhao, Peng and colleagues, 2016) used importance sampling to make rare crash and conflict events more frequent in simulation and then reweight the results statistically.

facts.text: University of Michigan researchers reported acceleration factors of roughly 300 to 100,000 for car-following crash evaluation using importance sampling.
facts.quote: They reported acceleration factors of roughly 300 to 100,000 for car-following crash evaluation

facts.text: University of Michigan researchers reported acceleration factors of 2,000 to 20,000 for lane-change conflict evaluation using importance sampling.
The University of Michigan accelerated crash and conflict evaluations are proofs of principle for on-road automated-driving behavior.
facts.quote: These are proofs of principle for on-road automated-driving behavior.

facts.text: The University of Michigan accelerated crash and conflict evaluations do not eliminate model validation or sensor and vehicle tests.
facts.quote: They do not eliminate model validation or sensor and vehicle tests

facts.text: No regulator accepted a production AEB on the basis of the University of Michigan accelerated crash and conflict evaluations.
facts.quote: no regulator accepted a production AEB on this basis

facts.text: The University of Michigan accelerated crash and conflict evaluations say nothing about perception failures caused by dust, snow, radar multipath from quarry walls, mud on lenses, articulation, bucket or boom occlusion, or sensor-position variation.
facts.quote: they say nothing about perception failures caused by dust, snow, radar multipath from quarry walls, mud on lenses, articulation, bucket or boom occlusion, or sensor-position variation.

facts.text: Foretellix reports that an anonymous Level 4 developer increased scenario coverage from 12 to 87 percent through six months of simulation-led process change.

facts.text: Foretellix reports that six months of simulation-led process change at an anonymous Level 4 developer shortened projected development from about 4.5 years to under two years.

facts.text: The customer in Foretellix's Level 4 developer case study is unnamed, and the reported scenario-coverage and projected-development figures are not independently verified.
